Boundary conditions

Source: R/boundary-conditions.R
dirichlet_bc.Rd

Boundary conditions are selected by boundary marker, never by coordinate comparisons.

Usage

dirichlet_bc(value = 0, marker = "boundary")

neumann_bc(flux = 0, marker = "boundary")

robin_bc(alpha, value = 0, marker = "boundary")

Arguments

value

Boundary value.

marker

Boundary markers; "boundary" selects the whole boundary.

flux

Outward flux k du/dn.

alpha

Robin coefficient (non-negative).

Value

An object of class pde_bc.

Details

  • dirichlet_bc(value, marker): u = value on the marked boundary. Enforced strongly by eliminating the boundary degrees of freedom and moving their contribution to the right-hand side, which keeps symmetric positive definite systems symmetric positive definite.

  • neumann_bc(flux, marker): k du/dn = flux (outward normal). Adds int flux v ds to the load.

  • robin_bc(alpha, value, marker): k du/dn + alpha u = value. Adds int alpha u v ds to the bilinear form and int value v ds to the load.

value, flux and alpha may be numbers, function(x, y) or, for time-dependent problems, function(x, y, t).

Dirichlet data are imposed by nodal interpolation at the boundary degrees of freedom. When several Dirichlet conditions share a degree of freedom (for example a corner), the condition listed last wins. A degree of freedom with a Dirichlet condition ignores Neumann and Robin contributions.

Examples

dirichlet_bc(0, "boundary")
#> <pde_bc> dirichlet on boundary 
neumann_bc(function(x, y) x, "top")
#> <pde_bc> neumann on top 
robin_bc(alpha = 2, value = 1, marker = "right")
#> <pde_bc> robin on right
